summary: A CCC-era steel tower in the Black Hills National Forest with conflicting build dates (1935-1942), last staffed in 1972 and now rented as a cabin.

facts.design: 67.5-foot steel tower, 7x7 cab, with separate log cabin living quarters
facts.status_note: tower is closed to public climbing; adjacent log cabin is rentable

staffing.status: last staffed 1972, now emergency detection only

access.note: log cabin open for rental via Recreation.gov; steel firetower itself is closed for public use

visit.trail_note: roads to the cabin not plowed, generally inaccessible December-March

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service - Black Hills National Forest, Elk Mountain Ranger District

events.note: firelookout.com describes a 40-foot wooden tower built in 1935, later moved to a meadow southeast of Moon Campground and destroyed in the early 1960s; this may be a separate, earlier structure rather than the current tower
Rapid City Journal (July 22, 1939) describes a newly built 67.5-foot steel tower at Summit Ridge, built shortly after Elk Mountain's tower, as a temporary high-danger station
NHLR dates the current structure to 1942, built by the CCC as a sister tower to Elk Mountain
Frank Lanouette staffed in 1952; Ralph Marshall staffed 1963-1966
last staffed in 1972; now used for emergency detection only
registered November 15, 1991 as US 31, nominated by District Ranger Burns L. Davison

evidence.supports: sister tower to Elk Mountain, 1942 build, CCC construction, 67.5ft steel tower with 7x7 cab and log cabin, last staffed 1972, restored, roof style differs from plans
evidence.quote: A sister tower to Elk Mountain, and located nine miles due north, Summit Ridge Lookout was built in 1942, also by the CCC. The 67.5' steel tower, with 7'x7' cab also has a log cabin living quarters. Last staffed in 1972, it is now used for emergency detection only. The Elk Mountain Ranger District has restored the facility.

evidence.supports: roof style deviation from construction plans
evidence.quote: The tower has a somewhat unusual roof style that is different than what was shown on its construction plans.
Date Registered November 15, 1991 ... Nominated by Burns L. Davison, District Ranger, USFS, Elk Mountain Ranger District

evidence.supports: 1939 newspaper account of newly built 67.5-foot steel tower, temporary high-fire-danger station, built shortly after Elk Mountain
evidence.quote: On the west side of the forest is the tower at Summit ridge, towering 6,100 feet above sea level. This tower was built shortly after the completion of the one at Elk mountain, and will be a temporary station to be manned only during times of great fire danger. The lookout is a 67 1/2 foot tower, located at the head of Roby canyon near the Wyoming line.

evidence.supports: 1935 wooden tower, moved and destroyed, 1939-1940 present tower built, known lookout personnel
evidence.quote: 1935: 40' wooden tower. Moved to a meadow southeast of Moon campground (tower destroyed early 1960s). Built from 1939-1940, the present tower is located less than 1/4 mile from the Wyoming border and is listed on the National Historic Lookout Register. Known lookout personnel: 1941-1947: Jessie Scott; 1952: Frank Lanouette; 1963-1966: Ralph Marshall.

evidence.supports: cabin rental details, tower closed to public, CCC-built cabin used as lookout personnel housing
evidence.quote: An accessible vault toilet is located on site and a steel firetower is located near the cabin, but is closed for public use.

evidence.supports: cabin built by CCC in 1930s as housing for lookout personnel
evidence.quote: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the 1930's, the cabin was originally used as housing for personnel that staffed the adjacent forest fire lookout tower.

evidence.supports: cabin sleeps 4 comfortably, reservable by groups up to 10, plus 2 RV sites available alongside it
evidence.quote: The cabin measures 22' x 32' and is comfortable for four people, though groups as large as ten may reserve the facility. ... Summit Ridge Lookout Cabin also has 2 RV sites at additional $12 each, allowing RVs up to 20 and 30 feet.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Four sources give different build years for the current steel tower: firelookout.com's '1935' appears to describe an earlier, separate 40-foot wooden tower that was later moved and destroyed, distinct from the present 67.5-foot steel tower. A contemporaneous 1939 newspaper describes the steel tower as newly built that year. firelookout.com separately dates 'the present tower' to 1939-1940. NHLR dates the current structure to 1942. The story presents all of these rather than picking one, since the sources may be describing the tower's construction (1939) versus completion/outfitting (1940-1942).

corrections.proposed: primary build likely 1939 (steel tower, contemporaneous newspaper) with NHLR giving 1942; 1935 appears to describe an earlier wooden tower moved elsewhere and destroyed, per firelookout.com
corrections.why: A 1939 Rapid City Journal article describes the 67.5-foot steel tower as newly constructed that year, and firelookout.com attributes the 1935 wooden tower to a different location/structure that was later destroyed, not the structure now listed on the NHLR.

sources.title: Forest Lookouts in the Black Hills

notes_for_editor: Build-date conflict across four sources (1935/1939/1939-40/1942) could not be fully resolved within the research budget; flagged in both story and corrections. Worth a closer look at NRHP/npgallery nomination documents if available, which might clarify construction vs completion dates.
